Frozen I1 admits a C3 model record only 'under the section 2.2 transfer clause', and that clause is CONJUNCTIVE: eligible only if the corpus can state what the record's own text says about its payoff support AND applicability conditions. A16 §(d) notices the divergence between that bar and X6's disjunctive bar, and resolves it by applying only X6 — i.e. by admitting a record whose abstract states EITHER an assumed environment OR a condition under which its result holds. The justification offered ('X-codes are the protocol's operative exclusion mechanism') does not engage with the fact that I1 is an INCLUSION criterion whose text carries the clause; failing an inclusion criterion is grounds for a non-include verdict independent of any X-code. Three mechanical consequences confirm the bar dropped rather than being applied: (a) 'payoff support' appears in exactly 5 of the 198 lines of the verdict file, and all five are in `undecided` rows — ZERO of the 178 include rows records the payoff support the clause requires the corpus to be able to state, so even the 'can state' precondition is unevidenced per record; (b) the `criterion_cited` field is an identical boilerplate string on every include row and asserts satisfaction of a clause no row substantiates; (c) ZERO X6 verdicts were returned, so inside the subset the only reachable exclusion code was X5 — the stage was structurally incapable of excluding any record on the transfer clause. This is the direct cause of the 178/197 = 90.4% include rate and of the corpus moving 149 -> 327, and it defeats A16 §(a)'s own stated reason for splitting SR-1 from the eligibility test ('no record could ever receive the one verdict the frozen protocol wrote for this literature'). A16 nevertheless asserts 'No eligibility criterion is altered.'

Those are different bars. **X6 as written in section 2.4 was applied**, because X-codes are the protocol's operative exclusion mechanism." — and the include rows' uniform warrant: "criterion_cited": "I1 via the section 2.2 transfer clause; I2 via C3; I3 satisfied by construction of the X11 stratum (the classifier routed records without a persistent identifier to X7); I4 satisfied at abstract depth"

Provenance verified myself: J4 begins at byte offset 19,899 of the file; I recomputed sha256 over the first 82,677 bytes and got 99524df02696a59ab878173ce7f3636d9cd07067b5a801a677cdf5d126fa13f4, matching the registered frozen-prefix digest (commit 27d7473, and the `_header` of both S4 log files). J4 defeats the finding's three load-bearing propositions:
1. "the stage never applied the clause's test" / "the bar dropped rather than being applied." J4 governs precisely this population - C3 model records on unbounded (non-2.1) instruments - and fixes its decision procedure as "the transfer clause in 2.2 plus X6." The clause's operative test, per the frozen protocol's own composition, IS the X6 test. Applying X6 is applying the clause, not substituting for it. 2. "failing an inclusion criterion is grounds for a non-include verdict independent of any X-code." Contradicted verbatim: "No separate judgement is exercised." J4 forecloses exactly the independent I1 judgement the finding demands.
3. "A16 nevertheless asserts 'No eligibility criterion is altered'" (offered as a false assertion). A16 lists "I1-I6, X1-X9, B-a-B-d, C1-C4 and J1-J6 are applied exactly as frozen in section 2." J4 is in that set, and A16 sec (d)'s reading is what J4 prescribes: state applicability conditions -> in; state neither -> X6. Under J4 the assertion is true.

The finding's cited reason for the SR-1 split is likewise preserved rather than defeated: J4's "state none and X6 applies" is literally "the one verdict the frozen protocol wrote for this literature," and A5 (lines 1449) had already reserved X6 as the code that "asserts the record states no applicability condition."
